amendments.old: CANONICAL DELIVERY SURFACE for garden ids: message, reply, or hand off to whoever an id names. The id alone does not say which rail that citizen answers on. Give target + intent; the decider picks transport from liveness (live socket citizen → control-socket send; deliverable self-fetch citizen → meta-bridge mailbox; probe-alive native-push citizen → direct injection into its conversation) and reports ONE outcome, named per rail: a control receiver's acceptance boundary (`sent` / `queued-steer` / `queued-follow-up` / `accepted-unknown-boundary` — those four, or `mailbox-enqueued` on a re-resolved mailbox leg), a mailbox ENQUEUE receipt, a native-push INJECTION, a rejection, or lock-dirty. This receipt is not the colleague's reply or evidence of reading. EXISTING targets only; discover with entwurf_peers. A live socket can receive fire-and-forget. unsupported means only "no control-socket probe," not reachability. The decider resolves the actual rail at dispatch time: a self-fetch mailbox only while deliverable, native-push direct injection only while its adapter probe is alive, or a THIRD RESULT: rejection when neither holds. An inactive self-fetch citizen is mailbox-undeliverable; native-push has NO mailbox: dead → native-push-target-dead; indeterminate → native-push-probe-indeterminate; agy (paused, #152) → native-push-paused, no probe. A dormant socket rejects this delivery verb as dormant-fire-forget-unsupported. owned-outcome was withdrawn. Only on an explicit operator request, entwurf_resume_call may visibly reopen a proven-dormant Pi, pi-durable or Claude Code citizen under the same id, submitting no prompt; that lifecycle is separate from delivery. LOCK: taken for a control-socket-DOMAIN dispatch. The mailbox and native-push rails are lock-free — deliverability and the adapter probe guard them. mode applies to a CONTROL-SOCKET send only; other plans carry no mode. wants_reply rides every rail. message caps at 16000 chars; send an artifact path + digest for more.
amendments.new: Send, reply or hand off to an existing garden id; the decider selects the live rail (live socket citizen → control-socket send; deliverable self-fetch citizen → meta-bridge mailbox; probe-alive native-push citizen → direct injection into its conversation) and reports ONE outcome, named per rail: a control receiver's acceptance boundary (`sent` / `queued-steer` / `queued-follow-up` / `accepted-unknown-boundary` — those four, or `mailbox-enqueued` on a re-resolved mailbox leg), a mailbox ENQUEUE receipt, a native-push INJECTION, a rejection, or lock-dirty. A receipt is not a reply or proof of reading. A local final is not delivery: when asked to reply, call entwurf_v2 for the requested recipient (normally the replyable sender); honor routing and no-send instructions. Discover existing targets with entwurf_peers. A live socket can receive fire-and-forget; unsupported means only "no control-socket probe," not reachability. For a target without a live socket, the THIRD RESULT is rejection if neither mailbox nor native-push is available. An inactive self-fetch citizen is mailbox-undeliverable; native-push has NO mailbox: dead → native-push-target-dead; indeterminate → native-push-probe-indeterminate; agy (paused) → native-push-paused, no probe. A dormant socket rejects this delivery verb as dormant-fire-forget-unsupported. This delivery verb never launches or resumes a process. Only on an explicit operator request, entwurf_resume_call may visibly reopen a proven-dormant Pi, pi-durable or Claude Code citizen under the same id, submitting no prompt; that lifecycle is separate from delivery. A control-socket-DOMAIN dispatch takes a target lock; mailbox and native-push rails are lock-free. mode applies only to a CONTROL-SOCKET send. wants_reply requests a response without authorizing an action or requiring an automatic acknowledgment; an absent or false marker does not cancel a request in the message. message caps at 16000 chars; send an artifact path + digest for more.

amendments.old: Send a message to an existing garden citizen by garden id through the entwurf-bridge (intent fire-and-forget). Returns the bridge's delivery receipt, or fails with its named rejection. This receipt is not the colleague's reply.
amendments.new: Send, reply or hand off to an existing garden id through entwurf-bridge (intent fire-and-forget), returning a delivery receipt or named rejection. The receipt is not a reply or proof of reading. For a requested reply, send to the authorized recipient, normally the replyable sender; a local final is not delivery. Honor routing and no-send instructions; an absent or false wants_reply does not cancel a request, and an address alone needs no ACK.

amendments.old: fire-and-forget = send/reply/hand-off to an existing target after a current rail check. unsupported is not a reachability verdict; the decider picks a rail or REJECTS (self-fetch → mailbox when deliverable, else mailbox-undeliverable; native-push → alive: direct injection, dead: native-push-target-dead, indeterminate: native-push-probe-indeterminate; a paused backend — agy, #152 — rejects as native-push-paused before any probe); set wants_reply to request an answer, not to wait for one. This is the ONLY intent: owned-outcome, which resumed a dormant citizen by launching a hidden background child, was withdrawn under the visible-first rule. It is not selectable, not deprecated-but-tolerated; a dormant socket citizen is currently unreachable by this verb and rejects as dormant-fire-forget-unsupported.
amendments.new: fire-and-forget sends, replies or hands off to an existing target after a current rail check. unsupported is not a reachability verdict: self-fetch uses a deliverable mailbox or rejects as mailbox-undeliverable; native-push injects when alive, rejects dead as native-push-target-dead and indeterminate as native-push-probe-indeterminate; paused agy rejects as native-push-paused before probing. wants_reply requests a response, not a wait. This delivery verb never launches or resumes a process; a dormant socket rejects as dormant-fire-forget-unsupported.
